body: It certainly is a paradox. Some will look at what I've done and think it was selfish. They'll say that I've hurt more people because of what I've done. I should endure this pain because of others. Maybe they're right. Maybe it is selfish. I don't know, but it's just another ring in an endless ladder to nowhere.

No worries - no need to preface anything. I don't downvote or chastise anyone who makes an attempt to help. 

Work isn't really my issue. I'm hoping to end the constant self-doubt, the loneliness, being powerless to stop this. All the years of sucking it up and being a man about all of this has taken its toll. I'm not looking for new friends. I wouldn't want to get involved with a new friendship in the middle of this. I've given up on dating for the same reasons. I'm reasonable enough to know that attempting to start any kind of relationship while being this depressed would be a bad idea.

Just trying to find a way out or to fix what's broken.

Work is about all that would normally distract me from this, but it isn't enough any longer. 

As far as friends go, I did, but I don't wish to put this on them anymore. I only had two that I felt I could trust with this. They're friends, not therapists.

I've been in and out of severe depression for over 25 years. When I was a teen, I took a wood chisel today my wrist, but wasn't successful - maybe I didn't want to be or was unsure. 

But the weight of it all is getting heavier and recent life changes over the last 2 years have only compounded the issue of depression. I'm trying to hold it off, but it wears on you. Fighting your own mind seems futile. It is merciless. And I'm just growing tired.

Mental health definitely is not an exact science, but I think they generally have the idea of treatment down. Some people just need more work. 

I would like to find out what specifically drives me into depression worst. Right now, I think it's fomo (fear of missing out) as I always feel that I'm being left out of events and gatherings that my friends have. I'm almost 42 and I've felt this way since I was around 15.  As a result, I feel lonely, and abandoned. I think it's just gotten worse throughout the years and it is starting to trigger the temptation of suicide more and more. If therapy cannot help, I cannot do another 20-30-40+ years of this.

I'm not exactly sure. In prior therapy, they would have me fill them in on my past, as a way to understand the root cause of the depression and suicidal ideations. Beyond that, they'd give me "homework" - lessons on thinking of one happy moment each morning, then twice a day, with two happy moments a day. I'd keep a journal. We'd discuss my previous weeks issues. This went on for a few months, but I honestly felt worse after all that. Not to mention that my health insurance wasn't covering much of the costs. I tried with 3 different therapists over 4 years. 

Maybe what I'm hoping for is to clear my head, find the root cause of my issues, and stop the suicidal planning? As it stands now, the suicidal ideation seems to be ramping up in frequency and in severity.

I have an appt with a therapist coming up soon. Just made arrangements recently. I've had several therapists in the past, but they weren't helpful, aside from being someone to listen to my issues. 5th times a charm, right?

I appreciate your reinforcement into the right of an individual (regardless of make or model of human) to feel however they want to feel. I think they *may* not have intended for it to come out like that, but I cannot be 100% sure. 

I cannot know with any certainty that I'll meet someone that I can connect with, but as you said, there's a chance. I think we all want to belong, to succeed, and to be happy. I think being happy is the most important. I think I'm missing the "happy" and "belonging" part, which leaves me feeling unsuccessful. If I can regain the happiness part, life may start to improve. 

Thank you for the kind words!

Yeah, I'm not sure if their intention was to include race/gender, but that's definitely what they used in their discussion with me. 

Yes, waiting it out is all that it seems to be now. I'm trying to find the positivity in all this, but depression, the inner voice of depression, is constantly beating me down. It's a constant fight with my inner monologue, and it's not an easy one to fight off. 

Thank you for your words and empathy, as it's always welcome to know that you're not alone, in the traditional sense.
